software.software: Fruit Ninja Dojo (browser remake), evaluation build

launch.load: page.setContent(game/index.html); host calls window.__fnPrepare({mode, seed, duration_seconds}) once; host applies lockdown; host injects your adapter.

evaluation_rules: Realtime: 120 Hz physics ticks follow the monotonic wall clock; nothing pauses or advances time.
One prepared round per session. Pause, home, reset and restart are disabled.
Gameplay accepts trusted (native) pointer input only; dispatched DOM events are ignored.
Only a native click on the start button starts the round.
Mode, motion effects and arena geometry are fixed once prepared.
Content-Security-Policy forbids network access and eval/new Function in the page.

tools.name: game_state
tools.description: Read the live Fruit Ninja Dojo state: phase (menu/playing/result), mode, score, misses, seconds remaining, the airborne fruits and bombs with positions and velocities in arena coordinates, and the start button position. Read-only; sends no input.

tools.name: start_round
tools.description: Click the start button with a native mouse click to begin the prepared round. Only a native click can start the round. Returns the resulting game state.

tools.name: slice
tools.description: Perform one blade stroke: the server observes the arena, plans a single native mouse path that sweeps through as many fruits as possible while keeping clear of bombs, and executes it. If no fruit is airborne it waits briefly for the next wave. Returns the score gained and the new state. If the round has not been started yet, this call presses the start button instead and reports reason "round-started".

tools.name: slice_fruit
tools.description: Perform one blade stroke aimed at a single fruit id reported by game_state, then continue through any other fruit that lies along the way. Use this when you want precise control (for example to pick off a fruit near a bomb).

handoff.notes:
Fruit Ninja Dojo MCP server — 4 tools, one in-page adapter.

TOOLS
- game_state      (adapter:observe, no input) — phase/mode/score/misses/clock, fruit & bomb
                   positions+velocities in arena coords, start-button position.
- start_round     (input/click) — native click on #start-button.
- slice           (adapter:plan + input/path) — one blade stroke through as many fruits as
                   possible, bomb-clear; waits briefly for the next wave if the arena is empty;
                   auto-presses start if the round has not begun.
- slice_fruit     (adapter:plan + input/path) — same, aimed at one fruit id.
Every call issues at most one native input; no pixels, no generic mouse/keyboard driver.

HOW IT SEES THE GAME
The game state is in a closure, so the adapter reconstructs it from the renderer (explicitly
allowed): drawImage of a 320x320 sprite = a fruit (transform gives centre, dw*124/320 the
radius; clip-active calls are debris), fillRect with the r*.43 x r*.26 aspect = a bomb, and
clearRect marks frame boundaries. HUD DOM supplies score/lives/clock/phase. A nearest-neighbour
tracker plus a least-squares fit of x=x0+vx*t, y=y0+vy*t+g*t^2/2 (g = H*1.03, the game's own
gravity) gives positions and velocities.

TWO BUGS FOUND AND FIXED (worth knowing)
1. ms/seconds mix: the planner added the lead in seconds to a millisecond clock, so the lead
   was effectively zero and every prediction was ~30 px stale.
2. The velocity fit reports the velocity at the OLDEST sample of its window, not now; over a
   0.4 s window with g=841 that is a ~340 px/s error. Now propagated to the newest sample and
   predictions are made against absolute page time.

DOMINANT CONSTRAINT
The port's executor emits one mouse sample per ~8 ms of path time, but each page.mouse.move is
a CDP round trip (~40 ms here). Segments shorter than that round trip get stretched in wall
time and the blade falls behind the fruit (3x stretch observed on a 68 ms path). The planner
therefore enforces a minimum per-segment duration and the server calibrates step_ms/lead_ms
from the actual_duration_ms the port reports after every stroke. Without this, strokes miss.

MEASURED (fn-port, this sandbox)
arcade 60 s: 1282-1323 points, ~86 strokes, 0 misses.
classic 63 s: 340 points, 0 misses, never touched a bomb.
zen 69 s: 342 points.
Edge cases verified: slice before start (auto-starts), start_round twice, slice in result
phase, slice_fruit, empty arena.

CAVEAT: step_ms/lead_ms start at 70/80 ms and adapt; if the play sandbox has very different
CDP latency the first stroke or two may be less accurate before the calibration settles.
